q: This poet asked "What happens to a dream deferred?" in a poem that begins "Harlem." He also wrote "The Negro Speaks of Rivers." He was a leading figure of the Harlem Renaissance. For 10 points, name this American poet.

This author's memoir I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings describes her childhood in Stamps, Arkansas. She read a poem at Bill Clinton's inauguration. She also wrote the poem "Still I Rise." For 10 points, name this American writer.

In this novella, an old Cuban fisherman named Santiago goes eighty-four days without catching a fish. He finally hooks a giant marlin and fights it for days, but sharks eat it on the way back to shore. For 10 points, name this short novel by Ernest Hemingway.

In this novel, the Joad family leaves their Oklahoma farm during the Dust Bowl and drives Route 66 to California. Tom Joad has just been released from prison, and Rose of Sharon gives birth to a stillborn baby. For 10 points, name this John Steinbeck novel.

In this novel, Guy Montag is a fireman whose job is to burn books. He meets a young neighbor named Clarisse and later escapes to join exiles who memorize books. The title is the temperature at which paper burns. For 10 points, name this dystopian novel by Ray Bradbury.

In this novel, a boy named Jonas is selected to be the Receiver of Memory in a community without color or pain. He learns about war, snow, and love, and later flees with a baby named Gabriel. For 10 points, name this Lois Lowry novel.

In this short story, the narrator insists he is not mad while describing how he killed an old man with a vulture-like eye. He hid the body under the floorboards but hears a heart beating louder and louder. For 10 points, name this Edgar Allan Poe story.

In this short story, a schoolteacher named Ichabod Crane is chased by a rider who throws a pumpkin at him. He competes with Brom Bones for the hand of Katrina Van Tassel. The title valley is near Tarrytown, New York. For 10 points, name this story by Washington Irving.

This play is set in 1692 Massachusetts, where girls led by Abigail Williams accuse villagers of witchcraft. John Proctor refuses to sign a false confession and is hanged. It is an allegory for McCarthyism. For 10 points, name this Arthur Miller play.

The Younger family in this play lives in a cramped Chicago apartment and debates how to spend a ten-thousand-dollar insurance check. Walter Lee wants to invest in a liquor store while his sister Beneatha wants to become a doctor. Its title comes from a Langston Hughes poem. For 10 points, name this Lorraine Hansberry play.

In this play, the Stage Manager narrates the lives of the people of Grover's Corners, New Hampshire. Emily Webb marries George Gibbs, then dies in childbirth and returns to relive one day. It is performed on a nearly bare stage. For 10 points, name this Thornton Wilder play.

In this novel, thirteen-year-old Brian Robeson survives alone in the Canadian wilderness after a plane crash. His only tool is a gift from his mother. For 10 points, name this Gary Paulsen novel named for a small axe.

In this novel, Stanley Yelnats is sent to Camp Green Lake, where boys must dig a hole five feet deep and five feet wide every day. He is cursed by his "no-good-dirty-rotten-pig-stealing-great-great-grandfather." He befriends Zero. For 10 points, name this Louis Sachar novel.

In this story, a lazy man falls asleep in the Catskill Mountains after drinking with strange men playing ninepins. He wakes up twenty years later with a long beard. For 10 points, name this Washington Irving story.

This book describes the author's two years living in a cabin near a Massachusetts pond. Chapters include "Economy," "Where I Lived, and What I Lived For," and "Sounds." Its author later wrote the essay "Civil Disobedience." For 10 points, name this work by Henry David Thoreau.
Answer these questions about Mark Twain.
parts: Mark Twain was the pen name of this man, who took the name from a riverboat term for water two fathoms deep.
In this Twain memoir, he recalls his days as a steamboat pilot on a great river.
In this Twain short story, Jim Smiley bets on a frog that has been filled with quail shot. Name this story set in Calaveras County.

q: Answer these questions about Edgar Allan Poe.
parts: Poe is often credited with inventing this genre of fiction through "The Murders in the Rue Morgue."
In this Poe story, a man bricks up his enemy Fortunato in a wine cellar. Name this story about a cask of wine.
This Poe story about Roderick and Madeline ends with a mansion splitting in two and falling into a tarn. Give its title.

q: Answer these questions about American poets.
parts: This poet and illustrator wrote the collection Where the Sidewalk Ends.
This Chicago poet wrote that "the fog comes on little cat feet."
This poet wrote "We Real Cool" and was the first Black author to win the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry.

q: Answer these questions about American science fiction and fantasy.
parts: In this Madeleine L'Engle novel, Meg Murry travels through space to rescue her father using a tesseract.
In this Kurt Vonnegut novel, Billy Pilgrim becomes "unstuck in time" after surviving the bombing of Dresden.
Ray Bradbury wrote this book of linked stories about human colonists on a neighboring planet.

q: Answer these questions about the Transcendentalists.
parts: Walden Pond is near this Massachusetts town, where many Transcendentalists lived.
This Transcendentalist wrote the essays "Nature" and "Self-Reliance."
This woman edited the Transcendentalist journal The Dial and wrote Woman in the Nineteenth Century.

q: Answer these questions about American plays.
parts: This Arthur Miller play about the Loman family features a salesman named Willy.
This Tennessee Williams play features Blanche DuBois and her brother-in-law Stanley Kowalski.
This Tennessee Williams play about the Wingfield family features a collection of tiny glass animals.

q: Answer these questions about Ernest Hemingway.
parts: This Hemingway novel follows expatriates including Jake Barnes from Paris to the bullfights of Pamplona.
In this Hemingway novel, ambulance driver Frederic Henry falls in love with nurse Catherine Barkley during World War One.
In this Hemingway novel, an American named Robert Jordan fights alongside Spanish guerrillas. Its title comes from a John Donne meditation.

q: Answer these questions about American short stories.
parts: In this Shirley Jackson story, villagers gather each June to draw slips of paper from a black box.
In this O. Henry story, a young couple sells their most prized possessions, a watch and long hair, to buy each other Christmas presents.
In this Charlotte Perkins Gilman story, a woman confined to a room becomes obsessed with the pattern on its walls.

q: In this play, three witches tell a general that he will become king, and his wife urges him to murder the sleeping Duncan. He later sees a floating dagger and the ghost of Banquo. He is finally killed by Macduff after Birnam Wood seems to move. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy.

In this play, the fairy king Oberon tells Puck to put a love potion on the eyes of Demetrius. Titania falls in love with Bottom, whose head has been turned into a donkey's. A group of craftsmen performs "Pyramus and Thisbe." For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy set in a forest near Athens.

In this play, Cassius persuades Brutus to join a conspiracy against the ruler of Rome. A soothsayer warns the title character to beware the Ides of March. Mark Antony then delivers a speech that begins "Friends, Romans, countrymen." For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which the title character says "Et tu, Brute?"

In this play, Bassanio borrows money from Shylock with his friend Antonio as guarantor. Portia disguises herself as a lawyer and argues that the contract allows a pound of flesh but no blood. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play set in an Italian city of canals.

This writer was born in Stratford-upon-Avon and married Anne Hathaway. His plays include comedies, histories, and tragedies, and he also wrote a sequence of 154 sonnets. He was a member of the Lord Chamberlain's Men. For 10 points, name this English playwright of Hamlet and Macbeth.

In this novel, an orphan raised in a workhouse famously asks, "Please, sir, I want some more." He falls in with Fagin and the Artful Dodger, who train boys as pickpockets. He is later threatened by Bill Sikes. For 10 points, name this Charles Dickens novel about a boy named Oliver.

In this novel, a blacksmith's apprentice named Pip is given money by a secret benefactor. He is cruelly treated by Estella, who is raised by Miss Havisham, a jilted bride who stopped all the clocks. The convict Magwitch turns out to be his benefactor. For 10 points, name this novel by Charles Dickens.

This novel opens with the line "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times." Set in London and Paris during the French Revolution, it features Madame Defarge, who knits the names of the doomed. Sydney Carton takes the place of Charles Darnay at the guillotine. For 10 points, name this Dickens novel.

In this novel, Elizabeth Bennet's first impression of the proud Mister Darcy is a bad one, and her sister Jane loves Mister Bingley. Lydia runs away with the soldier Wickham. It begins with the line that a single man with a fortune must want a wife. For 10 points, name this Jane Austen novel.

In this book, the animals of Manor Farm drive out Mister Jones and live by the Seven Commandments. The pigs Napoleon and Snowball fight for power, and the horse Boxer works himself to death. It ends with "All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others." For 10 points, name this allegory by George Orwell.

In this novel, Jim Hawkins finds a map in the chest of the old pirate Billy Bones at the Admiral Benbow Inn. He sails on the Hispaniola and meets the one-legged cook Long John Silver. Ben Gunn has been marooned on the island. For 10 points, name this Robert Louis Stevenson adventure novel.

In this novella, the lawyer Mister Utterson investigates the connection between a respectable doctor and a vicious man who trampled a girl. The doctor has been drinking a chemical mixture that transforms him. For 10 points, name this Robert Louis Stevenson novella about a split personality.

In this novel, a detective from Baker Street investigates the death of Sir Charles at Baskerville Hall on Dartmoor. A giant glowing creature is said to haunt the moor, but it is really a dog used by Stapleton. For 10 points, name this Arthur Conan Doyle novel starring Sherlock Holmes.

This fictional detective lives at 221B Baker Street and plays the violin. He is assisted by Doctor Watson and battles his enemy Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls. He is known for the line "Elementary." For 10 points, name this detective created by Arthur Conan Doyle.

In this novel, a man is shipwrecked and lives on an island for twenty-eight years. He saves a man from cannibals and names him for the day of the week on which he was found. For 10 points, name this Daniel Defoe novel about a castaway.

In this novel, Lemuel Gulliver visits Lilliput, where the people are six inches tall, and Brobdingnag, where they are giants. He later meets the intelligent horses called Houyhnhnms. For 10 points, name this satire by Jonathan Swift.

In this novel, Jonathan Harker visits a castle in Transylvania and later meets Van Helsing. Mina Harker is bitten by a count who sleeps in a coffin of earth. The novel is told through letters and diary entries. For 10 points, name this Bram Stoker novel.

In this novel, cylinders crash near Woking and release creatures from Mars who travel in giant tripod machines. The narrator watches them destroy London until they are killed by bacteria. For 10 points, name this H. G. Wells science fiction novel.

In this novel, an inventor travels to the year 802,701 and meets the gentle Eloi, who are preyed on by the Morlocks. He is helped by a young woman named Weena. For 10 points, name this H. G. Wells novel.

This theater was home to the Lord Chamberlain's Men and stood in London on the south bank of the Thames. A fire started by a cannon during a performance of Henry VIII destroyed the first one in 1613. For 10 points, name this circular theater where many Shakespeare plays premiered.

In this play, a professor of phonetics bets his friend Colonel Pickering that he can pass a Cockney flower girl off as a duchess. Eliza Doolittle learns to speak proper English. It was adapted as the musical My Fair Lady. For 10 points, name this George Bernard Shaw play.

In this collection of stories, a boy raised by wolves is taught the Law of the Jungle by the bear Baloo and the panther Bagheera. He is hunted by the tiger Shere Khan. For 10 points, name this Rudyard Kipling book about Mowgli.

In this play, Viola is shipwrecked in Illyria and disguises herself as the page Cesario. Countess Olivia falls for Viola, while Duke Orsino loves Olivia. Malvolio is tricked into wearing yellow stockings. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare comedy.

This book was written by Sir Thomas Malory and printed by William Caxton. It tells of Lancelot, Guinevere, Merlin, and the Round Table. The title translates as "The Death of Arthur." For 10 points, name this French-titled collection of tales about the legendary king.

In this novel, a boy raised in Suffolk meets the kind Mister Micawber, the "umble" Uriah Heep, and his stern aunt Betsey Trotwood. He is friends with Steerforth and marries Dora. For 10 points, name this Dickens novel about a boy who becomes a writer.

In this novel, a handsome young man's portrait ages and grows hideous while he stays young. Lord Henry Wotton influences him, and the painter Basil Hallward is killed. For 10 points, name this Oscar Wilde novel about a man named Dorian.

This novel is set in a future World State in which babies are grown in bottles and sorted into castes such as Alphas and Epsilons. The citizens take a drug called soma, and a man called the Savage is brought from a reservation. For 10 points, name this Aldous Huxley dystopian novel.

In this poem, the speaker sees a "crowd, a host, of golden" flowers beside a lake, fluttering and dancing in the breeze. It was inspired by a walk in the Lake District. For 10 points, name this poem by William Wordsworth that begins "I wandered lonely as a cloud."

In this poem, a sailor stops a wedding guest and tells him about a voyage. After he shoots a large seabird, the ship is becalmed, and he laments "Water, water, every where." For 10 points, name this Samuel Taylor Coleridge poem about a sailor who is cursed.

This poem begins "Tyger Tyger, burning bright, in the forests of the night." It asks what immortal hand or eye could frame the animal's fearful symmetry. It is a companion to "The Lamb." For 10 points, name this William Blake poem about a large cat.
Answer these questions about Shakespeare's tragedies.
parts: This Shakespeare play features a prince of Denmark and the line "To be, or not to be."
In this Shakespeare play, an aging king divides his kingdom among his daughters Goneril and Regan, but disowns Cordelia.
In this Shakespeare play, Iago manipulates a Moorish general into thinking his wife Desdemona has been unfaithful.

q: Answer these questions about Jane Austen.
parts: In this Austen novel, a matchmaking young woman from Highbury meddles in the love lives of her friends.
In this Austen novel, the sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood experience heartbreak.
In this Austen novel, Catherine Morland imagines a Gothic mystery at a certain abbey.

q: Answer these questions about Romantic poets.
parts: This poet wrote "Ozymandias," about a ruined statue in the desert.
This poet wrote "Ode on a Grecian Urn" and "To Autumn" before dying young of tuberculosis.
This poet of the Victorian era wrote "The Charge of the Light Brigade" and "Ulysses."

q: Answer these questions about Shakespearean characters.
parts: This wife of a Scottish thane urges her husband to murder the king and later cannot wash imaginary blood from her hands.
This villain of Othello is the general's ensign who plots his downfall.
This fat, boastful knight is a friend of Prince Hal in the Henry IV plays and appears in The Merry Wives of Windsor.

q: Answer these questions about George Eliot.
parts: George Eliot was the pen name of this woman.
In this Eliot novel set in a provincial town, Dorothea Brooke marries the scholar Casaubon.
In this Eliot novel, a weaver in Raveloe finds a golden-haired child by his fire after his gold is stolen.

q: Answer these questions about Thomas Hardy.
parts: In this Hardy novel, a poor girl from Wessex is seduced by Alec and later marries Angel Clare.
In this Hardy novel, a stonemason named Jude Fawley dreams of studying at a university city called Christminster.
In this Hardy novel, Michael Henchard sells his wife and later becomes the mayor of a Dorset town.

q: Answer these questions about early English writers.
parts: This man wrote The Canterbury Tales.
This Elizabethan playwright wrote Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine.
This blind poet wrote Paradise Lost.

q: Answer these questions about Agatha Christie.
parts: Christie created this Belgian detective with a waxed mustache.
In this Christie novel, Poirot investigates a murder aboard a train stopped by a snowdrift.
In this Christie novel, ten strangers are lured to Soldier Island and killed one by one.

q: In this novel, an aging Spanish gentleman reads so many tales of chivalry that he renames his horse Rocinante and sets out as a knight. He attacks windmills that he believes are giants and is accompanied by his squire Sancho Panza. He dedicates his deeds to Dulcinea. For 10 points, name this novel by Miguel de Cervantes.

In this novel, Jean Valjean is imprisoned for nineteen years for stealing a loaf of bread and is relentlessly pursued by the inspector Javert. He adopts Cosette, the daughter of Fantine. The story climaxes at a barricade during the 1832 Paris uprising. For 10 points, name this novel by Victor Hugo.

In this novel, the bell ringer Quasimodo is deaf and deformed and lives in a cathedral in Paris. He rescues the Gypsy dancer Esmeralda from the archdeacon Claude Frollo. For 10 points, name this Victor Hugo novel set at Notre-Dame.

In this novel, the young Gascon d'Artagnan travels to Paris and befriends Athos, Porthos, and Aramis. They battle the forces of Cardinal Richelieu and the spy Milady de Winter. Their motto is "All for one, and one for all." For 10 points, name this Alexandre Dumas novel.

In this novel, a young sailor named Edmond Dantès is falsely imprisoned in the Château d'If. He learns of a hidden treasure from the Abbé Faria and later takes revenge under a noble title. For 10 points, name this Alexandre Dumas novel about a man who becomes a wealthy count.
In this novel, Professor Aronnax, his servant Conseil, and the harpooner Ned Land are captured by Captain Nemo. They travel in the submarine Nautilus. For 10 points, name this Jules Verne novel.

In this novel, Phileas Fogg wagers fellow members of the Reform Club that he can circle the globe in the time given in the title. He travels with his servant Passepartout and is trailed by the detective Fix. For 10 points, name this Jules Verne novel.

In this book, a pilot crashes in the Sahara and meets a boy from a tiny asteroid. The boy talks about a rose he loves and a fox who asks to be tamed. It contains the line "What is essential is invisible to the eye." For 10 points, name this novella by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry.

These two German brothers, Jacob and Wilhelm, collected tales from storytellers and published them as Children's and Household Tales. Their collection includes "Rumpelstiltskin," "Snow White," and "Rapunzel." For 10 points, name these scholars of fairy tales.

In this fairy tale, a little girl named Gerda sets out to rescue her friend Kai, who has a splinter of a troll's mirror in his eye. They are separated by a ruler of a frozen palace. For 10 points, name this Hans Christian Andersen tale that inspired a Disney film.

In this fairy tale, two swindlers claim to weave cloth that is invisible to people who are unfit for their jobs. A child in a crowd finally says the ruler has nothing on. For 10 points, name this Hans Christian Andersen story.

In this fairy tale, an odd baby bird is mocked by the farm animals because he is big and gray. After a hard winter, he sees his reflection and realizes he is a swan. For 10 points, name this Hans Christian Andersen story.

In this novella, a traveling salesman wakes up one morning transformed into a giant insect. His sister Grete eventually stops caring for him, and his father throws apples at him. For 10 points, name this story about Gregor Samsa by Franz Kafka.

This novel follows the Rostov and Bolkonsky families during the French invasion of Russia in 1812. Characters include the idealistic Pierre Bezukhov, Prince Andrei, and Natasha. For 10 points, name this very long novel by Leo Tolstoy.

In this novel, a woodcarver named Geppetto carves a puppet that comes to life. The puppet's nose grows when he lies, and he is swallowed by a sea creature. His conscience is a talking cricket. For 10 points, name this novel by Carlo Collodi.

In this play, a swordsman with a huge nose helps the handsome Christian win the love of Roxane by writing letters in his name. He dies after being hit on the head by a log. For 10 points, name this Edmond Rostand play about a poet and soldier.

In this novel, an orphan girl is sent to live with her grandfather in the Swiss Alps and befriends the goatherd Peter. She is later taken to Frankfurt to keep company with Clara, who uses a wheelchair. For 10 points, name this Johanna Spyri novel about a girl.

The title girl of this book has red braids, super strength, and a horse. She lives at Villa Villekulla with a monkey named Mister Nilsson, and befriends Tommy and Annika. For 10 points, name this Astrid Lindgren book series about a Swedish girl.

In this novel, a masked figure lives beneath the Paris Opera House and tutors the singer Christine Daaé. He drops a chandelier and loves Christine despite her love for Raoul. For 10 points, name this Gaston Leroux novel.

This book was written by a Jewish girl who hid in a secret annex above her father's office in Amsterdam. She addressed entries to an imaginary friend named Kitty. For 10 points, name this diary by Anne Frank.

In this novel by Johann Wyss, a shipwrecked pastor and his wife and four sons build a home in a giant tree on a tropical island. The father narrates their efforts to survive with animals and plants. For 10 points, name this novel about a stranded family.

In this story by E. T. A. Hoffmann, Marie receives a wooden toy from her godfather Drosselmeier. The toy comes to life and defeats the Mouse King. Tchaikovsky based a famous ballet on it. For 10 points, name this Christmas story about a toy soldier who cracks nuts.

In this novel by Michael Ende, a boy named Bastian steals a book from a bookstore and reads it in his school attic. He is pulled into the land of Fantasia and aids the young warrior Atreyu. For 10 points, name this German children's fantasy that features a luckdragon named Falkor.

In this novel, Paul Bäumer and his classmates enlist after a teacher's patriotic speeches. They face death at the front in World War One. It ends as Paul is killed on a day when the army report notes nothing new. For 10 points, name this Erich Maria Remarque novel.

This Finnish author wrote and illustrated books about a family of white trolls living in a valley, including Finn Family Moomintroll. The characters include Snufkin and Little My. For 10 points, name this author of the Moomin series.

In this short story by Nikolai Gogol, a poor clerk named Akaky Akakievich saves for months to buy a new garment. It is stolen, and he dies after a powerful person refuses to help him. His ghost then snatches coats in Saint Petersburg. For 10 points, name this story named for a piece of clothing.

This seventeenth-century French author collected fairy tales such as "Cinderella," "Puss in Boots," and "Sleeping Beauty." His book was published as Tales of Mother Goose. For 10 points, name this author who gave Cinderella her glass slipper.

This series of comic albums by the Belgian artist Hergé follows a young reporter with a tuft of hair. His dog is Snowy, and his friends include Captain Haddock and Professor Calculus. For 10 points, name this reporter whose adventures include The Blue Lotus.

This comic series by René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo follows a Gaulish village that resists Roman conquest. The warriors drink a magic potion brewed by the druid Getafix. The hero's large friend Obelix carries menhirs. For 10 points, name this series about a small warrior.

In this fairy tale collected by the Brothers Grimm, a brother and sister leave a trail of breadcrumbs that birds eat. They find a house made of sweets and escape a witch by pushing her into an oven. For 10 points, name this fairy tale.
Answer these questions about Russian authors.
parts: This author wrote Anna Karenina, which begins with a line about happy and unhappy families.
This author's novel Crime and Punishment follows Raskolnikov, a student who murders a pawnbroker.
This playwright wrote The Cherry Orchard and Three Sisters.

q: Answer these questions about French authors.
parts: This Enlightenment writer wrote Candide, a satire in which a young man is taught that this is the best of all possible worlds.
This Algerian-born author wrote The Stranger and The Plague and won the Nobel Prize in 1957.
This author wrote the seven-volume novel In Search of Lost Time, and is famous for the narrator tasting a madeleine dipped in tea.

q: Answer these questions about German authors.
parts: This author wrote the play Faust and the novel The Sorrows of Young Werther.
This author wrote Death in Venice and The Magic Mountain.
This author wrote Siddhartha and Steppenwolf.

q: Answer these questions about Scandinavian writers.
parts: This Danish author wrote "The Little Mermaid."
This Norwegian playwright wrote A Doll's House, in which Nora leaves her husband.
This Swedish playwright wrote Miss Julie and The Dance of Death.

q: Answer these questions about Spanish writers.
parts: This author wrote Don Quixote.
This poet and dramatist wrote Blood Wedding and Poet in New York and was killed at the start of the Spanish Civil War.
This seventeenth-century dramatist wrote Life Is a Dream.

q: Answer these questions about Italian writers.
parts: This author of the Divine Comedy is guided through hell by Virgil.
This author wrote the Decameron, in which ten young people tell stories to escape the plague in Florence.
This poet wrote a sequence of sonnets to a woman named Laura.

q: Answer these questions about Jules Verne.
parts: In this Verne novel, Professor Lidenbrock and his nephew Axel descend into a volcano in Iceland.
In this Verne novel, three men are fired toward the lunar surface from a giant cannon.
In this Verne novel, a group of balloonists from the American Civil War end up on an island with Captain Nemo.

q: Answer these questions about European folk tales.
parts: In this tale, a musician in a colorful coat lures rats from a town in Lower Saxony with his pipe, then leads away the children when he is not paid.
In this Grimm tale, a donkey, a dog, a cat, and a rooster set out to become musicians and scare off robbers.
In this French tale, a wealthy man with a strange-colored facial hair kills his wives and forbids the latest to open a certain room.

q: In this novel, Okonkwo is a proud wrestler in the Igbo village of Umuofia who accidentally kills a clansman. After being exiled, he returns to find that British missionaries and colonial officials have changed his community. His son Nwoye converts to Christianity. For 10 points, name this novel by Chinua Achebe.

In this novel, an Andalusian shepherd boy named Santiago has a recurring dream about treasure near the Pyramids. He meets a king named Melchizedek, falls in love with Fatima in the desert, and learns to listen to his heart. For 10 points, name this novel by the Brazilian author Paulo Coelho.

In this collection, a queen named Scheherazade tells her husband a story every night so that he will not execute her. The stories include the voyages of Sinbad the Sailor. For 10 points, name this collection of Middle Eastern folk tales, whose title includes the number one thousand and one.

In this novel, Amir betrays his friend Hassan, a Hazara servant, during a kite-fighting tournament in Kabul. Years later, he returns to Afghanistan to rescue Hassan's son Sohrab. For 10 points, name this novel by Khaled Hosseini.

This graphic memoir follows the author as a girl in Tehran during the Islamic Revolution. She is later sent to school in Vienna. It was written and drawn in black and white by Marjane Satrapi. For 10 points, name this autobiographical comic.

In this novel, a boy named Piscine Molitor Patel survives a shipwreck on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker. Its author is the Canadian writer Yann Martel. For 10 points, name this novel about a boy adrift in the Pacific.

This memoir recounts how a teenager and his father, Shlomo, survive the concentration camps at Auschwitz and Buchenwald. It begins in the town of Sighet in Transylvania. For 10 points, name this short book by Elie Wiesel.

In this Chinese novel, the monk Xuanzang travels to India to retrieve Buddhist scriptures. He is protected by Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, along with Pigsy and Sandy. For 10 points, name this novel attributed to Wu Cheng'en.

This work, written by the court lady Murasaki Shikibu, is often called one of the world's first novels. It follows the "Shining Prince" and is set in the Heian court of Japan. For 10 points, name this work named for its hero, Hikaru.

In this Sanskrit epic, Prince Rama is exiled to the forest with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana. Sita is kidnapped by the demon king Ravana, and Rama enlists the monkey god Hanuman to rescue her. For 10 points, name this Hindu epic attributed to Valmiki.

In this Mesopotamian epic, the king of Uruk becomes friends with the wild man Enkidu and battles the monster Humbaba. After Enkidu dies, the hero seeks the immortal Utnapishtim, who survived a great flood. For 10 points, name this epic about a Sumerian king.

This sacred book of the K'iche' Maya tells of the Hero Twins, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, who defeat the lords of the underworld Xibalba. It also describes how humans were created from maize. For 10 points, name this Mayan text of Guatemala.
This Chilean poet wrote Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair and many odes to common things like socks and tomatoes. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971. For 10 points, name this poet.

This thirteenth-century Persian poet founded the Mevlevi order, whose followers whirl in a ritual dance. He wrote the Masnavi and lived in Konya. For 10 points, name this mystic poet whose verses are widely read in English translation.

This collection of quatrains was written by a Persian mathematician and astronomer and translated into English by Edward FitzGerald. It includes the line "A Jug of Wine, a Loaf of Bread, and Thou." For 10 points, name this work of Omar Khayyam.

In this Latin epic, the hero flees the burning city of Troy and lands in Carthage, where Queen Dido falls in love with him. He fights Turnus in Italy. For 10 points, name this epic by Virgil that tells of the founding of Rome.

In this Greek tragedy, a plague strikes Thebes, and the king learns that he killed his father and married his mother. Jocasta hangs herself, and the king blinds himself. For 10 points, name this play by Sophocles.

This ancient Greek storyteller is credited with fables such as "The Tortoise and the Hare" and "The Boy Who Cried Wolf." Each of his tales ends with a moral. For 10 points, name this legendary author.

In this novel, the Zulu minister Stephen Kumalo travels from his village to Johannesburg to search for his son Absalom. It was published in 1948. For 10 points, name this novel whose title is a plea for a land.

In this memoir, a comedian describes growing up in South Africa during apartheid as the son of a Black mother and a white father. His mother Patricia is a major figure. For 10 points, name this book by Trevor Noah whose title refers to the illegality of his birth.

In this memoir, a girl from the Swat Valley of Pakistan describes being shot by the Taliban for speaking out about girls' education. It was coauthored with Christina Lamb. For 10 points, name this book by a Nobel Peace Prize winner.

In this Mexican novel, Tita is forbidden to marry Pedro and pours her emotions into cooking. Each chapter begins with a recipe. For 10 points, name this novel by Laura Esquivel whose title describes water at the point of boiling.

This seventeenth-century Japanese poet perfected the haiku and wrote a travel diary called The Narrow Road to the Deep North. His most famous poem describes a frog jumping into an old pond. For 10 points, name this poet.

This Bengali writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection Gitanjali. He founded a school at Santiniketan and wrote the lyrics of the national anthems of India and Bangladesh. For 10 points, name this poet.

This Sanskrit epic, attributed to Vyasa, is one of the longest poems ever written. It tells of a war at Kurukshetra between the Pandavas and the Kauravas. It contains the Bhagavad Gita. For 10 points, name this Indian epic.

This eighteenth-century Chinese novel follows the decline of the Jia family. It features Jia Baoyu and Lin Daiyu and is also called The Story of the Stone. For 10 points, name this novel by Cao Xueqin.

In this memoir, a twelve-year-old girl in Shanghai wants to join the Red Successors but her family is labeled as having a bad background. It describes the Cultural Revolution. For 10 points, name this memoir by Ji-li Jiang.

In this novel, Mariam and Laila become wives of the abusive Rasheed in Kabul. It follows the two women through decades of conflict in Afghanistan. For 10 points, name this novel by Khaled Hosseini whose title is from a poem.

This ancient Greek poet, traditionally said to have been blind, composed two epics about the Trojan War and its aftermath. They feature the heroes Achilles and Odysseus. For 10 points, name this poet.

This autobiography describes how the author grew up in a Xhosa village, became a lawyer, and was sentenced at the Rivonia Trial. He spent years on Robben Island before becoming president of South Africa. For 10 points, name this memoir by Nelson Mandela.
Answer these questions about Greek dramatists.
parts: This tragedian wrote Medea, in which a woman takes revenge on Jason.
This author wrote the Oresteia trilogy, which includes Agamemnon.
This comic playwright wrote Lysistrata and The Frogs.

q: Answer these questions about African writers.
parts: This author wrote Things Fall Apart and was born in the Igbo town of Ogidi.
This Nigerian playwright won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986 and wrote Death and the King's Horseman.
This Kenyan author wrote Weep Not, Child and A Grain of Wheat, and for years wrote in the Gikuyu language.

q: Answer these questions about Latin American writers.
parts: This Colombian author wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude, set in the town of Macondo.
This Chilean poet was the first Latin American woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, and she wrote Desolación.
This seventeenth-century Mexican nun wrote the poem "First Dream" and defended women's right to education in her Reply.

q: Answer these questions about Chinese philosophers and poets.
parts: This sage's sayings were collected in the Analects.
This legendary figure is credited with the Tao Te Ching.
This Tang dynasty poet wrote "Quiet Night Thought" and was famous for his love of wine and the moon.

q: Answer these questions about Japanese literature.
parts: This short Japanese poem has three lines of five, seven, and five syllables.
This woman wrote a famous novel set in the Heian court about Prince Genji.
This author wrote I Am a Cat and Botchan and appears on an older Japanese banknote.

q: Answer these questions about the literature of India.
parts: This ancient collection of animal fables was written in Sanskrit to teach princes how to rule.
In this section of the Mahabharata, the warrior Arjuna receives advice from Krishna before a battle.
This classical Sanskrit dramatist wrote Shakuntala and the poem The Cloud Messenger.

q: Answer these questions about writers from the Middle East.
parts: This Lebanese-American poet wrote The Prophet, a book of essays in verse.
This Egyptian novelist, who won the 1988 Nobel Prize, wrote the Cairo Trilogy.
This Turkish novelist, who won the 2006 Nobel Prize, wrote My Name Is Red and Snow.

q: Answer these questions about Roman poets.
parts: This Roman poet wrote the Metamorphoses, a collection of myths about transformations.
This Roman poet's Odes include the phrase "carpe diem."
This Roman poet wrote love poems to a woman he called Lesbia.

q: In this novel, Gandalf and thirteen dwarves led by Thorin Oakenshield recruit a homebody to help reclaim a treasure guarded by a dragon. The hero wins a magic ring in a riddle contest with Gollum. For 10 points, name this novel by J. R. R. Tolkien about Bilbo Baggins.

In this novel, four siblings enter a magical land through a wardrobe in a professor's house. Edmund betrays the others for Turkish delight, and the White Witch keeps the land in perpetual winter. A lion sacrifices himself at the Stone Table. For 10 points, name this book by C. S. Lewis, the first published in the Chronicles of Narnia.

In this novel, a girl follows a white rabbit with a pocket watch down a hole. She attends a tea party with the Mad Hatter, plays croquet with flamingos, and meets a Queen who shouts "Off with her head!" For 10 points, name this Lewis Carroll novel.

In this play, Wendy, John, and Michael Darling fly with the title boy to the Neverland. They fight the pirate Captain Hook, who is chased by a crocodile that swallowed a clock. Tinker Bell drinks poison meant for the hero. For 10 points, name this J. M. Barrie play about a boy who never grows up.

In this novel, Charlie Bucket wins one of five golden tickets to tour a factory run by Willy Wonka. Other winners include Augustus Gloop and Veruca Salt. The Oompa-Loompas work in the factory. For 10 points, name this Roald Dahl novel about a sweet-making plant.

In this novel, a brilliant girl reads at a library and discovers she can move objects with her mind. She is mistreated by her car-salesman father and by the headmistress Miss Trunchbull. Miss Honey is her kindly teacher. For 10 points, name this Roald Dahl novel.

In this book, a boy named Christopher Robin lives with a bear who loves honey and has a friend named Piglet. Other animals in the Hundred Acre Wood include Eeyore and Tigger. For 10 points, name this A. A. Milne book about a bear of very little brain.

In this novel, a Mole meets a Water Rat, and they have adventures with Badger and a rich, reckless amphibian who loves motor cars. Toad Hall is eventually retaken from weasels. For 10 points, name this Kenneth Grahame novel set on a riverbank.

In this novel, Mary Lennox is sent from India to live at Misselthwaite Manor in Yorkshire. She finds a locked, overgrown garden and befriends Dickon and her sickly cousin Colin. For 10 points, name this Frances Hodgson Burnett novel.
In this book, a mischievous bunny wearing a blue jacket sneaks into Mister McGregor's garden. His siblings are Flopsy, Mopsy, and Cottontail. For 10 points, name this Beatrix Potter book.

In this picture book, Max is sent to bed without supper after wearing a wolf suit. He sails to an island and becomes king of creatures with terrible claws. Max says "Let the wild rumpus start!" For 10 points, name this Maurice Sendak book.

In this picture book, a tiny creature hatches from an egg on a Sunday and eats through one apple on Monday, two pears on Tuesday, and so on. After a stomachache, it forms a cocoon. For 10 points, name this Eric Carle book.

In this novel, a boy discovers he is the son of Poseidon and is accused of stealing Zeus's master bolt. He attends Camp Half-Blood with Annabeth and Grover. For 10 points, name this Rick Riordan novel, the first in the Percy Jackson series.

In this novel, Katniss Everdeen volunteers to take her sister Prim's place in a televised fight to the death. She represents District 12 alongside Peeta Mellark. For 10 points, name this Suzanne Collins novel set in Panem.

In this novel, Frodo Baggins inherits a ring and sets out with eight companions to destroy it in the fires of Mount Doom. Sauron is its dark lord. For 10 points, name this epic fantasy trilogy by J. R. R. Tolkien.

In this novel, a boy named August Pullman, who has a facial difference, starts fifth grade at Beecher Prep. His teacher Mister Browne teaches precepts, including that one should choose kindness. For 10 points, name this R. J. Palacio novel.

This novel is narrated by a horse who describes his early life on a farm and his hard years pulling cabs in London. His friends include Ginger and Merrylegs. For 10 points, name this Anna Sewell novel.
This sound device repeats the same consonant sound at the start of nearby words. "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers" is a tongue twister that uses it. For 10 points, name this device.
"I've told you a million times" and "I'm so hungry I could eat a horse" are examples of this figure of speech. It uses deliberate exaggeration for emphasis. For 10 points, name this figure of speech.
This fourteen-line poem is written in iambic pentameter. The Petrarchan form has an octave and a sestet, while Shakespeare's form ends with a rhyming couplet. For 10 points, name this form of poem.
This five-line humorous poem has an AABBA rhyme scheme and is often nonsense. Edward Lear popularized it. For 10 points, name this form that can begin "There once was a man from Nantucket."

In its verbal form, a speaker says the opposite of what is meant. In its situational form, an outcome is the reverse of what is expected. In its dramatic form, the audience knows something that a character does not. For 10 points, name this literary device.
This device uses hints early in a story to suggest what will happen later. An author might use a storm cloud or a character's omen to create it. For 10 points, name this narrative technique.

In literature, this term refers to the main character of a story, who is often opposed by an antagonist. The word comes from Greek for "first actor." For 10 points, name this term for a story's central character.

In this kind of story, the characters, settings, and events represent ideas such as virtue or vice. Pilgrim's Progress is a famous example. For 10 points, name this type of narrative with a hidden symbolic meaning.

In this genre, authors imagine a society in which people suffer under oppressive control, as in The Giver and Fahrenheit 451. It is the opposite of a utopia. For 10 points, name this genre of science fiction.
Answer these questions about Roald Dahl.
parts: In this Dahl book, a young girl named Sophie is carried off by a giant who blows dreams into children's bedrooms.
In this Dahl book, a boy escapes his awful aunts by climbing into a huge fruit pulled by seagulls.
In this Dahl book, a clever animal steals chickens and cider from three mean farmers named Boggis, Bunce, and Bean.

q: Answer these questions about classic picture books.
parts: In this Margaret Wise Brown book, a young bunny says goodnight to everything in a great green room.
In this Robert McCloskey book, a family of birds waddles through Boston to reach the Public Garden.
In this Crockett Johnson book, a boy draws his own adventures with a drawing tool.

q: Answer these questions about Tolkien's Middle-earth.
parts: This wizard with a gray cloak and a pointed hat guides Bilbo and Frodo.
This creature, who loves his "precious," was once a hobbit named Sméagol.
This hidden valley, home to Elrond, is the "Last Homely House" east of the Misty Mountains.

q: Answer these questions about poetry.
parts: This term refers to a group of lines in a poem, like a paragraph in prose.
This metrical pattern has five unstressed-stressed feet per line, and it is used in sonnets and blank verse.
This term describes a sentence that runs over from one line of a poem to the next without a pause.

q: Answer these questions about science fiction.
parts: In this Orson Scott Card novel, a gifted boy named Andrew Wiggin is trained at Battle School.
In this Frank Herbert novel, Paul Atreides moves to a desert planet that produces the spice melange.
In this Douglas Adams novel, Arthur Dent escapes Earth's destruction with a friend named Ford Prefect.

q: Answer these questions about children's authors.
parts: This author wrote about Ramona Quimby and Henry Huggins.
This author wrote Tales of a Fourth Grade Nothing and Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret.
This author wrote Tuck Everlasting, about a family that drank from a spring and never ages.

q: Answer these questions about children's mystery series.
parts: This teenage detective from River Heights solves mysteries in books credited to Carolyn Keene.
These two brothers, Frank and Joe, solve crimes in a series credited to Franklin W. Dixon.
This boy detective from Idaville solves cases for a dime a day, with the help of Sally Kimball.

q: Answer these questions about Lewis Carroll's works.
parts: This animal with a wide grin disappears bit by bit, leaving only its smile.
This nonsense poem from Through the Looking-Glass describes the slaying of a beast, with "frabjous" and "galumphing."
In this poem, an oysters-eating pair walk on a beach, and a Walrus and a Carpenter weep.

q: This king of Corinth was punished in the underworld for cheating death. He was forced to push a huge boulder up a hill, only to watch it roll back down each time it neared the top. For 10 points, name this figure whose name now describes an endless, futile task.

This god was born on the island of Delos after his mother Leto was refused shelter by most lands. He killed the serpent Python at Delphi, and he flayed the satyr Marsyas after a music contest. He drove the sun chariot in some later traditions and led the Muses. For 10 points, name this twin brother of Artemis, the Greek god of music, prophecy, and healing.

This god ruled the sky and wielded thunderbolts forged by the Cyclopes. He overthrew his father Cronus with the help of his siblings. He lived on Mount Olympus with his wife Hera. For 10 points, name this king of the Greek gods.

This goddess sprang fully grown from the forehead of her father after he swallowed her mother Metis. She competed with Poseidon to become patron of a city and gave it the olive tree. Her symbols include the owl and the aegis. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of wisdom and warfare, patron of Athens.

This god was granted rule over the sea in a three-way division of the world with his brothers. He created the first horse by striking the ground with his weapon. He carries a trident. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea and earthquakes.

This goddess is the wife and sister of Zeus and is often angered by his affairs. She sent snakes to attack the infant Heracles in his crib. Her sacred animal is the peacock. For 10 points, name this Greek queen of the gods and goddess of marriage.

This goddess was the twin sister of Apollo and was born on Delos. She hunts with a silver bow and is accompanied by deer. She turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

This god was the lover of Aphrodite and was the son of Zeus and Hera. His sons Phobos and Deimos, whose names mean fear and panic, accompanied him into battle. His Roman counterpart is Mars. For 10 points, name this Greek god of war.

This goddess was born from sea foam near the island of Cyprus. She promised Paris the most beautiful woman in the world as a reward in a famous contest. Her son is Eros. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of love and beauty, called Venus by the Romans.

This god was thrown from Olympus by his mother and became lame. He built the thunderbolts of Zeus, the armor of Achilles, and a golden net that trapped his wife. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the forge and blacksmiths.

This god wears winged sandals and a winged hat and carries a staff entwined with two snakes called the caduceus. He guided souls to the underworld and delivered messages for Zeus. For 10 points, name this Greek messenger god.

This goddess was grief-stricken when her daughter was abducted, causing a famine on the earth. She taught Triptolemus the art of agriculture. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the harvest and mother of Persephone.

This god was raised by nymphs after being born from the thigh of Zeus. He was worshipped with wild festivals and was accompanied by satyrs and maenads. Grapevines and ivy were sacred to him. For 10 points, name this Greek god of wine.

This god ruled the underworld and wore a helmet that made him invisible. He abducted Persephone to be his queen. His realm was guarded by a three-headed dog. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the dead.

This goddess ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld and so had to return there for part of every year. Her yearly return from below was said to bring spring. For 10 points, name this daughter of Demeter, queen of the underworld.

This hero was set twelve labors by King Eurystheus as punishment for killing his own family in a fit of madness. He wore the skin of the Nemean lion. For 10 points, name this strongest of the Greek heroes.

This hero killed Medusa by looking only at her reflection in a polished shield. He rescued Andromeda from a sea monster. He was born after Zeus came to his mother Danae as a shower of gold. For 10 points, name this Greek hero.
This hero navigated the Labyrinth of Crete with the help of a ball of thread from Ariadne. He was the son of King Aegeus of Athens. For 10 points, name this slayer of the Minotaur.

This hero spent ten years trying to return to Ithaca after the Trojan War. He blinded the Cyclops Polyphemus and resisted the song of the Sirens. His wife Penelope waited for him. For 10 points, name this protagonist of Homer's Odyssey.

This warrior was dipped into the River Styx by his mother Thetis, leaving only his heel vulnerable. He sulked in his tent after a quarrel with Agamemnon and later killed Hector. For 10 points, name this greatest Greek warrior of the Trojan War.
This monster had snakes for hair and turned anyone who looked at her into stone. She was one of three Gorgon sisters, though the only mortal one. For 10 points, name this monster beheaded by Perseus.

This monster had the head of a bull and the body of a man. It was kept in a maze built by Daedalus and was fed young people sent from Athens. For 10 points, name this creature of Crete, killed by Theseus.

Epimetheus ignored his brother's warning and married this woman, who was given a gift by the gods that she was told never to open. Her curiosity led her to lift the lid of a large storage jar, and sorrows and diseases escaped, leaving only hope behind. For 10 points, name this first woman of Greek myth.

This Titan stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans. As punishment, Zeus chained him to a rock where an eagle ate his liver each day. For 10 points, name this Titan whose name means forethought.

This musician played a lyre so beautifully that animals and trees followed him. He went to the underworld to retrieve his wife Eurydice but lost her when he looked back. For 10 points, name this legendary Greek poet and musician.
This king of Phrygia was granted a wish by Dionysus, and everything he touched turned to gold. He later was given donkey ears by Apollo. For 10 points, name this king with the golden touch.
This young man ignored his father's warning and flew too close to the sun with wings made of feathers and wax. The wax melted and he fell into the sea. For 10 points, name this son of Daedalus.
This winged horse sprang from the blood of Medusa when she was beheaded. It was ridden by Bellerophon when he killed the Chimera. For 10 points, name this flying horse of Greek myth.

This creature was the offspring of the monsters Typhon and Echidna. It had a serpent for a tail and was often shown as a three-headed dog. Souls could enter its master's realm but could not leave past it, and Heracles dragged it to the surface as his final labor. For 10 points, name this guardian of the underworld.
